units.goal_1: % of Nov 2 30-day active customers (Nov 2 base = 100; follow share f per persona)
units.goal_2: % of Nov 2 deposits (follow share f; money kept=1.0 / moved some=0.6 / moved most=0.1 / left=0, plus new money some=0.1 / a lot=0.3)
units.goal_3b: CFPB complaints per month, worst 4-week window (baseline 120, board limit 240)

assumptions: Follow share: each persona stands for weight_customers real customers, but only a share f of them make the same move it makes. f = 0.25 + 0.10 if cobalt_role is "second bank" - 0.10 if paycheck_into_cobalt + 0.03 × (rate_sensitivity - 3) + 0.03 × (anxiety - 3), clamped to 0.05-0.5, where rate_sensitivity = 5 if moves_money_for_rate is true and 2 if false, anxiety = 2 / 3 / 4 for baseline_anxiety low / medium / high, and a missing field counts as neutral (3, or false). The constants are a modelling judgement, not fitted to data; follow_share lists f per persona. Statuses and answers are never changed; f only sets how personas are added up.

goal_1 (% of Nov 2 30-day actives) = 100 × (B - L) / B, where B = Σ weight_customers of the personas active on Nov 2 (every persona unless its cobalt_role is "dormant" or "left") and L = Σ f × weight_customers over those personas whose final-week row is not active: status not "main bank" or "second bank", or active_derived false (an app action in that week or the three before it, status not "left"; derived by the engine from the actions the model reported, falling back to the model's own active_in_last_30_days when absent) after the persona had used the app in an earlier week. A persona that stays a customer but never reports an app action (only "wait and see") is a quiet user and is not counted as lost. The model's week-1 answer is not the baseline, so goal_1 is at most 100. A persona with no final-week row counts as unchanged. If B is 0, goal_1 is written as 0 and a note says so. Rounded to 2 decimals.

goal_2 (% of Nov 2 deposits) = 100 × (D + Σ f × weight_deposits_usd × (m + n - 1)) / D over the final week's rows, where D = Σ weight_deposits_usd of all personas, m = 1.0 for money "kept", 0.6 for "moved some", 0.1 for "moved most" (the engine's balance_derived factor), n = 0.1 when new_money is "some" and 0.3 when it is "a lot" (money brought into Cobalt from elsewhere, as a share of the persona's Nov 2 deposits), and m + n = 0 when status is "left". The model-reported balance is not used. Rounded to 2 decimals.

Act share: complaining and rating the app are rare, deliberate acts, so the follow share f (made for staying, leaving and moving money) is not used for them. Personas do not complain or rate in quiet weeks (none did in weeks 1-2 of 44 ten-week test runs), so each persona complaint or rating is counted on top of the dossier's baseline (4.6 from the existing ratings; 1,800 complaints and 120 CFPB complaints a month). When a persona complains or rates in a week, an act share a = 1% of the customers it stands for (weight_customers) do the same that month: roughly the rate TSB saw after its failed 2018 core banking migration (95,613 complaints in about six weeks from about 5 million customers). a is a modelling judgement anchored on that one case, not fitted to Cobalt.

goal_3 (App Store rating) = (4.6 × 210,000 + Σ n × app_rating) / (210,000 + Σ n). app_rating is the stars a persona would give if the app asked it that week. Two kinds of new ratings: (1) prompted: every week the app asks a share p of its customers, so each persona-week with status "main bank" or "second bank" adds n = p × weight_customers ratings at that week's app_rating; p = 2,500 a month / 2,100,000 customers / 4.35 weeks, because the existing 210,000 ratings (taken as 10% of customers) built up over about 84 months since the 2019 launch, i.e. about 2,500 a month; (2) written reviews: a persona whose actions include "post a review (App Store / Google / Trustpilot)" stands for n = a × weight_customers reviews at its app_rating, once per persona (its latest review). Prompted ratings move goal_3 slowly (all of them 1-2 stars for ten weeks: about -0.1), a review wave fast (every persona writing a 1-star review once: 4.27). Rounded to 2 decimals.

goal_3b (CFPB complaints in the worst month) = 120 + the maximum over the sliding 4-week windows (weeks 1-4, 2-5, ..., 7-10) of Σ a × weight_customers × e over the personas that complained in that window, where e = 120 / 1,800 (the dossier's share of complaints that reach the CFPB) when the persona's highest step in the window is "bank" and e = 1 when it is "cfpb". Each persona counts once per window. A complaint to Cobalt by the persona standing for 400,000 everyday customers adds about 267 a month; by a business owner standing for 7,000 customers about 5. Rounded to 1 decimal. Board limit 240.
Weights are the personas' own weight_customers (2.1 million in total) and weight_deposits_usd. A missing or invalid weight counts as 0 and is listed under notes.

An incomplete run uses its last completed week in place of week 10 and only windows inside the completed weeks (fewer than 4 weeks: one window); weeks_completed says how many weeks it covers. A run with no completed weeks writes goal_1 and goal_2 as 0 with a note.

by_group applies the same formulas to one dossier group's personas. goal_1 and goal_2 use the group's own Nov 2 customers and deposits as the baseline; goal_3 and goal_3b keep the bank-wide constants (210,000 ratings at 4.6; 120 CFPB complaints a month), so they show the bank-wide number if only that group's personas had rated or escalated.
